question: Which specialist helps patients regain the ability to swallow safely?

options.A: Speech-language pathology
options.B: Occupational therapy
options.C: Respiratory therapy
options.D: Physical therapy

explanation: Spot on. Speech therapists evaluate and treat swallowing issues (dysphagia) to keep patients safe from choking or aspiration. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is the best way to help a patient stick to their long-term blood pressure medication plan?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop taking pills whenever their blood pressure normalizes
options.B: Explaining that the medication controls the condition rather than curing it
options.C: Insisting that family members administer every daily dose orally
options.D: Warning the patient that stopping pills causes instant cardiac arrest

explanation: Fantastic! Patients often stop taking meds when they feel fine. Teaching them that the drugs are keeping their pressure under control helps them stay consistent for life. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T2#GNS223_U1_T2_h8)

question: What is the main job of the ovaries in the female body?

options.A: Storing urine before it reaches the bladder
options.B: Producing eggs and female hormones
options.C: Filtering waste from the lower abdomen
options.D: Producing red blood cells during pregnancy

explanation: You got this! The ovaries are our female reproductive glands that make ova (eggs) and important hormones like estrogen and progesterone. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h1)

question: What do physical therapists mainly focus on during rehabilitation?

options.A: Fine motor coordination and cooking skills
options.B: Emotional coping and mental health support
options.C: Large muscle movements and lower body walking
options.D: Speech articulation and swallowing safety

explanation: Think of PTs as the experts on big movements! They focus on large muscles, balance, walking, and helping patients move around safely. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h4)

question: A doctor orders 250 mg of a suspension. The bottle label says 125 mg per 5 mL. How much should you measure?

options.B: 10 mL
options.C: 5 mL
options.D: 2.5 mL

explanation: Nice calculation! Dose ordered (250) divided by stock dose (125) equals 2. Multiply that by 5 mL, and you get 10 mL. You're getting the hang of this! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h3)

question: In clinical nursing, what is a 'toxidrome'?

options.A: An antidote given to reverse the effects of a specific snake venom
options.B: A group of signs and symptoms pointing to a specific class of poison
options.C: The physical damage caused by corrosive chemicals on the skin
options.D: The laboratory test used to measure blood alcohol concentration

explanation: Think of a toxidrome as a symptom 'syndrome' caused by a 'toxic' substance. It helps nurses quickly spot what kind of poison is at play! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T1#GNS215_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which everyday or routine activity carries a real risk of transmitting HIV?

options.A: Sharing eating utensils and drinking cups at a family dinner
options.B: Sharing intravenous drug injection needles with an infected person
options.C: Receiving a hug or handshake from an infected coworker
options.D: Swimming in the same public pool as a person with HIV

explanation: HIV spreads through direct blood-to-blood contact, such as sharing needles. Casual contact like hugging or sharing spoons is completely safe! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h3)

question: Why is it important for healthcare workers to understand the basic economics of food pricing?

options.A: It prevents nurses from ever having to worry about patient dietary budgets
options.B: It allows clinics to set direct retail prices for medications and supplies
options.C: It explains how economic shifts directly impact household nutrition and health outcomes
options.D: It qualifies nurses to manage local agricultural farms and crop yields

explanation: Understanding financial pressures helps clinicians recognize why patients might struggle to afford healthy diets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h1)

question: When is the very first (baseline) needle count done during a procedure?

options.A: When the patient is rolling out of the recovery room
options.B: After the surgeon has closed the skin incision
options.C: Before the surgery begins during instrument setup
options.D: Only when an emergency X-ray is requested

explanation: Fantastic! We always do a baseline count before any cut is made so we know exactly what we started with. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is the main reason our bodies have cavities protecting internal organs?

options.A: To produce blood cells for the immune system
options.B: To increase total body weight and maintain posture
options.C: To safeguard delicate internal organs from physical trauma
options.D: To control the rate of voluntary muscle movement

explanation: Body cavities act as natural physical shields that enclose and protect your vital organs from sudden bumps and movements. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T2#GNS111_U1_T2_h5)

question: What major problem must nurses watch out for after an infant goes through a difficult resuscitation?

options.A: Permanent closure of the ductus arteriosus
options.B: Hypoglycemia and temperature instability
options.C: Sudden onset of infantile colic
options.D: Excessive weight gain over the first day

explanation: Resuscitated babies burn through their sugar reserves very quickly and have a hard time staying warm, so checking blood sugar and temperature is vital. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h7)

question: What is the largest organ system in the human body?

options.A: Gastrointestinal system
options.B: Integumentary system
options.C: Respiratory system
options.D: Musculoskeletal system

explanation: Great start! The integumentary system covers your entire body and includes your skin, hair, and nails. Think of it as your body's ultimate protective suit—and yes, it's our biggest organ system! [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why must a nurse carefully inspect the skin over a joint before an intraarticular injection?

options.A: To determine the best clothing size for the patient
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the surrounding muscle
options.C: To check if the patient has any permanent tattoos on the limb
options.D: To make sure there is no active skin infection that could spread into the joint

explanation: Injecting through broken or infected skin carries bacteria straight into the sterile joint space, causing severe infection. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h5)

question: What should you do immediately if your patient starts coughing violently and turning blue while you are passing a tube?

options.A: Ask the patient to take a deep breath and swallow
options.B: Push the tube down faster to clear the way
options.C: Stop pushing and pull the tube right back out
options.D: Inject water to wash it down

explanation: Coughing and turning blue (cyanosis) means the tube has mistakenly slipped into the windpipe instead of the food pipe. Pull it back out immediately and let them catch their breath! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is the perineal body such an important structure in the pelvic floor?

options.A: It prevents the baby's head from descending too quickly into the pelvis.
options.B: It acts as a central meeting point for multiple pelvic floor muscles.
options.C: It directly controls the hormonal changes that trigger uterine contractions.
options.D: It produces the lubricating fluids needed during the second stage of labour.

explanation: You can picture the perineal body as a strong anchor point where several key muscles meet to support the pelvic organs and keep everything working smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h1)

question: Which pregnancy hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing the valve between the stomach and food pipe?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body to make room for baby, which also loosens the sphincter keeping stomach acid down. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h2)

question: Which type of medication is often prescribed to help manage chronic nerve pain?

options.A: Loop diuretics like furosemide
options.B: Inhaled short-acting beta-agonists
options.C: Broad-spectrum oral antibiotics
options.D: Anticonvulsants like gabapentin

explanation: Even though they were first made for seizures, anticonvulsants calm down wild, overactive nerve firing, making them great for shooting and burning nerve pain! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h6)

question: What is the most common long-term result for patients who receive radioactive iodine treatment?

options.A: The need for lifelong maintenance doses of propylthiouracil
options.B: Spontaneous recovery of normal thyroid function within five years
options.C: Complete physical removal of the thyroid gland through scarring
options.D: Permanent hypothyroidism requiring lifelong hormone replacement

explanation: Because the radiation quiets down the gland so well, many patients end up with an underactive thyroid and take daily thyroxine tablets. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T3#GNS223_U7_T3_h4)

question: What does informed consent require before a client receives a contraceptive method?

options.A: Proof of employment and stable monthly income
options.B: A written letter of approval from a community chief
options.C: Complete agreement from the client's extended family
options.D: Full understanding of benefits, risks, and correct usage

explanation: Informed consent means the client knows what to expect, including how the method works and its potential side effects, before they choose it. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h4)

question: What actually happens during DOTS (Directly Observed Therapy) for a TB patient?

options.A: A health worker watches the patient swallow every dose
options.B: Blood tests are run daily to measure drug levels in the serum
options.C: The patient reports their pill intake via phone once a week
options.D: Family members check the pill bottles at the end of each month

explanation: Under DOTS, a healthcare worker physically watches the patient take their meds to ensure they finish the whole course without missing days. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why do we always keep raw meat separate from ready-to-eat foods?

options.A: To speed up the cooking process
options.B: To improve the overall taste of the meal
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of cooking
options.D: To prevent cross-contamination of harmful bacteria

explanation: Think of it like keeping bad company away from good! Separating raw meat stops dangerous germs from jumping onto foods that won't be cooked again before eating. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h2)

question: Which disease is most commonly caught through accidental needle stick injuries in the clinic?

options.A: Malaria
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Typhoid fever
options.D: Hepatitis B

explanation: Hepatitis B is very easily spread through contaminated sharps in the hospital. This is why safety with needles is a huge deal for every nurse! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h2)

question: If a patient comes in with severe, nonstop vomiting and diarrhea, what electrolyte drop should you expect?

options.A: Low levels of white blood cells
options.B: Low levels of potassium and sodium
options.C: High levels of calcium and magnesium
options.D: High levels of red blood cells

explanation: Gut fluids are packed with electrolytes. Losing them rapidly from either end drains your sodium and potassium stores fast. Great clinical reasoning! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T11#GNS121_U2_T11_h6)

question: How can community health nurses help traditional practitioners who perform FGM?

options.A: Help provide alternative means of livelihood so they stop cutting
options.B: Force them to leave the community without any financial help
options.C: Ignore their economic needs and threaten them with jail only
options.D: Hire them in the hospital clinic to perform minor surgeries

explanation: Great job! Many practitioners rely on FGM to make a living, so teaching new skills and providing other sources of income helps them stop permanently. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T1#GNS225_U6_T1_h7)

question: How do corticosteroids stop swelling and inflammation in the body?

options.A: By blocking nerve impulses that transmit localized pain signals
options.B: By freezing cell membranes to prevent white blood cells from moving
options.C: By directly neutralizing circulating bacteria in the bloodstream
options.D: By altering DNA transcription to stop inflammatory chemical production

explanation: Steroids go right into cell nuclei to switch off the genes that create inflammatory chemicals. That's how they calm down swelling at the root! [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h2)

question: What is another common medical name for synovial fluid aspiration?

options.A: Arthrocentesis
options.B: Paracentesis
options.C: Thoracentesis
options.D: Lumbar puncture

explanation: Arthrocentesis specifically refers to puncturing a joint space to remove fluid for testing or pain relief. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h1)

question: In financial management, what is a "variance"?

options.A: The variation in patient recovery times across different wards
options.B: The difference between budgeted amounts and actual financial outcomes
options.C: The total amount of profit made from pharmacy sales alone
options.D: The legal penalty given to hospitals for missing safety records

explanation: A variance is simply the gap between what you planned to spend in your budget and what you actually spent in reality. [learn more](GST321_U1_T23#GST321_U1_T23_h5)

question: A patient eats plenty of carbs but lacks B-complex vitamins. What is likely to happen?

options.A: Cells struggle to release energy from those carbohydrates
options.B: The kidneys start filtering out all the extra glucose
options.C: The patient instantly develops severe muscle wasting
options.D: Blood sugar levels drop to zero within a few minutes

explanation: Exactly! Without B-vitamins acting as helpers, your cells have a hard time unlocking the energy trapped inside the food you eat. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h4)

question: Which nursing action shows an unconscious bias against an older patient?

options.A: Speaking slowly and using baby talk when explaining a medication
options.B: Providing written discharge instructions in large print
options.C: Reviewing the medical history with the patient's adult child present
options.D: Asking the patient about their preferred food choices for lunch

explanation: Using baby talk assumes older adults can't understand normal speech. We always want to treat our patients with full dignity! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T10#GNS324_U3_T10_h1)

question: What is considered the gold standard procedure for directly viewing pelvic structures and measuring tubal length?

options.A: Abdominal X-ray
options.B: Routine urinalysis
options.C: Transabdominal ultrasound
options.D: Diagnostic laparoscopy

explanation: Laparoscopy lets the surgeon look directly inside the pelvis with a tiny camera, making it the best way to check out the fallopian tubes up close. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h6)

question: When a mother of young children is admitted to the hospital for major surgery, what is the most likely effect on her family?

options.A: Family members will immediately stop working to stay in the hospital room.
options.B: Household expenses will decrease due to reduced grocery shopping.
options.C: The family structure remains entirely unchanged during hospital stays.
options.D: Family roles must be rearranged to cover childcare and household duties.

explanation: Spot on! When a key caregiver falls ill, family routines get disrupted, forcing other members to step up and handle chores and childcare. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h7)

question: When should you inspect the outside of the ear (the auricle)?

options.A: Only after the otoscopic examination is fully completed
options.B: While cleaning cerumen out of the middle ear space
options.C: Before inserting the speculum into the ear canal
options.D: Immediately after removing the pneumatic bulb attachment

explanation: Always check the outside of the ear first for any tenderness or sores before putting anything into the canal. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h5)

question: When planning a community program to prevent rickets in toddlers, which two nutrients should you focus on?

options.A: Sodium and Potassium
options.B: Iron and Vitamin C
options.C: Calcium and Vitamin D
options.D: Vitamin A and Zinc

explanation: Brilliant! Calcium and Vitamin D are best friends when it comes to building strong, hard bones and preventing rickets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h3)

question: A nurse is assessing a patient with a fractured lower leg. Which finding indicates compromised blood flow distal to the injury?

options.A: Strong swelling and severe localized pain
options.B: Warm skin and brisk capillary refill
options.C: Cool skin and a weak pedal pulse
options.D: Red discoloration around the ankle joint

explanation: Cool extremities, weak pulses, and delayed capillary refill point to blocked or reduced arterial blood flow past the fracture site. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the role of the fimbriae at the end of the fallopian tubes?

options.A: Catch the released egg from the ovary
options.B: Produce estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Secrete mucus to block foreign bacteria
options.D: Anchor the uterus to the pelvic wall

explanation: Fimbriae are fringe-like fingers that wave over the ovary at ovulation to sweep the egg inside the fallopian tube. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h5)

question: How does FGM commonly affect a woman's sexual health later in life?

options.A: It has zero impact on sexual function or emotional wellbeing
options.B: It can cause painful intercourse and reduced sexual sensitivity
options.C: It increases sensitivity and enhances sexual pleasure
options.D: It only affects fertility without altering sexual sensations

explanation: You're doing great! Because sensitive nerve endings and tissues are damaged or removed, many women face pain and decreased sensation. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T1#GNS225_U6_T1_h5)

question: What primary change in the maternal circulatory system causes physiological hemodilution during pregnancy?

options.A: Red blood cell production completely stops during the third trimester
options.B: Blood vessels shrink in diameter to speed up flow
options.C: Total body water decreases while iron stores multiply
options.D: Plasma volume increases much more than red blood cell mass

explanation: The fluid portion of blood expands significantly faster than actual red blood cells are manufactured, creating a dilutional effect. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h2)

question: When handing over a critical patient, what does the acronym SBAR stand for?

options.A: Safety, Behavior, Analysis, Response
options.B: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Airway, Respiration
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: System, Burden, Action, Review

explanation: SBAR is your best friend for smooth handovers. Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation keeps everything short, sweet, and safe! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T8#GNS321_U2_T8_h7)

question: A patient finishing treatment is terrified the cancer will return. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Promise them that cancer never, ever comes back
options.B: Tell them to stop thinking about their health history
options.C: Acknowledge their fear and discuss healthy coping and follow-up plans
options.D: Refer them for emergency surgery immediately

explanation: Fear of a comeback is completely normal for survivors. Validating their feelings and showing them the clear follow-up plan brings real peace of mind. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T9#GNS311_U2_T9_h9)

question: What is one of the common hurdles community health nurses face while working in many Nigerian settings?

options.A: Complete absence of public health problems to solve
options.B: Strict prohibition against working with local families
options.C: An overwhelming excess of modern medical equipment
options.D: Infrastructural deficits and resource constraints

explanation: You're doing amazing! Nigerian community nurses are true champions; they often navigate rough roads, limited supplies, and tough logistics to bring care to those who need it most. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T9#GNS225_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is a vital nursing action when feeding a patient who has trouble swallowing?

options.A: Avoid checking the mouth after meals
options.B: Provide only large dry food portions
options.C: Keep the patient in an upright position
options.D: Encourage the patient to lie flat quickly

explanation: Gravity is your best friend here! Keeping your patient upright helps food travel down safely and protects their lungs from accidental choking or aspiration. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of giving medications to clients with inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: To prevent family members from developing the same condition
options.B: To completely repair the damaged DNA inside the cells
options.C: To relieve specific symptoms and improve day-to-day comfort
options.D: To permanently stop the natural progression of the disease

explanation: Medications target troubling symptoms like spasms, pain, and stiffness to make the client more comfortable. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h4)

question: Which family planning method also protects against sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Progestin-only pills
options.B: Subdermal hormone implants
options.C: Copper intrauterine devices
options.D: Barrier methods

explanation: Condoms and other barrier methods are great because they do double duty: they prevent pregnancy and block infections too! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h3)

question: What is the main goal of Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) in public health?

options.A: To promote positive and healthy behaviour choices
options.B: To replace modern medicine with traditional remedies
options.C: To distribute free medical equipment to hospitals
options.D: To punish communities that ignore health guidelines

explanation: Spot on! BCC is all about working together with individuals and communities to help them build healthier lifestyle habits. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why might a nurse relax a patient's long-standing diabetic diet restrictions during palliative care?

options.A: Sugar has no effect on blood glucose in terminal patients
options.B: Strict dietary control is no longer relevant to their comfort and quality of life
options.C: Diabetes automatically cures itself in advanced illness
options.D: Patients with terminal illnesses can no longer taste sweetness

explanation: You nailed it! Chronic disease rules are meant for long-term health. In palliative care, bringing a smile with a sweet treat matters much more. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T17#GNS321_U4_T17_h4)

question: What is the medical term for the body returning its reproductive and pelvic organs back to normal after childbirth?

options.A: Atrophy
options.B: Hyperplasia
options.C: Involution
options.D: Metaplasia

explanation: Brilliant! Involution is just the body's wonderful natural process of shrinking and healing back to its pre-pregnancy state. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T12#GNS121_U5_T12_h4)

question: Who is known as the father of nutrition for his early work on how our bodies use oxygen to burn food for energy?

options.A: James Lind
options.B: Casimir Funk
options.C: Antoine Lavoisier
options.D: Hippocrates

explanation: Correct! Lavoisier used clever chemical experiments to show how respiration and metabolism tie directly into how we process food. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h3)

question: What is the main goal of applied research in healthcare?

options.A: To prove that hospitals do not need nurses
options.B: To replace all medical textbooks completely
options.C: To solve a specific, practical clinical problem
options.D: To explore ideas with no real-world use

explanation: Great thinking! Applied research focuses directly on fixing real, everyday problems we face in practice, like figuring out how to reduce ward infection rates. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the function of the flexible plastic canulas used in an MVA kit?

options.A: To seal the outside opening of the vagina during suction
options.B: To travel through the cervix and vacuum out uterine tissue
options.C: To measure the exact internal temperature of the uterus
options.D: To pump local anesthetic pain medicine into the cervix

explanation: Canulas are the sterile tubes inserted past the cervix into the uterus to channel the suctioned tissue into the syringe. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard contraindication for an intravenous pyelogram?

options.A: Severe kidney failure
options.B: Known allergy to iodine dye
options.C: Mild seasonal pollen allergy
options.D: Confirmed pregnancy

explanation: Allergies to pollen do not interfere with iodine contrast dye, whereas iodine allergies, kidney failure, and pregnancy are major contraindications. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main job of the hypothalamus in your body?

options.A: Maintaining internal balance and homeostasis
options.B: Producing voluntary skeletal muscle movement
options.C: Filtering visual images from the optic nerve
options.D: Processing high-level abstract mathematical thoughts

explanation: Well done! The hypothalamus acts like your body's thermostat and control center, constantly checking temperature, water balance, and chemistry to keep you stable. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T19#GNS211_U3_T19_h3)

question: When we talk about extracellular fluid (ECF) outside our cells, what are its two main parts?

options.A: Intracellular fluid and plasma
options.B: Cerebrospinal fluid and synovial fluid
options.C: Intracellular fluid and interstitial fluid
options.D: Intravascular fluid and interstitial fluid

explanation: Nice try! ECF is basically the fluid inside your blood vessels (plasma) plus the fluid resting right between your tissues (interstitial fluid). You're mastering body fluids step by step! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T11#GNS121_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why must a nurse shake a suspension oral medication before pouring a dose?

options.A: To create bubbles that improve the taste
options.B: To warm the liquid up to body temperature
options.C: To evenly redistribute the settled drug particles
options.D: To activate the chemical preservatives inside

explanation: Suspensions contain solid particles that naturally settle at the bottom of the container, so shaking ensures the patient gets the correct dose strength. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which drug class works by acting as faulty building blocks that trick the reverse transcriptase enzyme?

options.A: Integrase Inhibitors
options.B: Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs)
options.C: Entry Inhibitors
options.D: Protease Inhibitors (PIs)

question: Why do public health teams create a clear 'case definition' during an outbreak?

options.A: To determine which pharmaceutical company supplies drugs
options.B: To decide clearly who is counted as having the outbreak disease
options.C: To write a legal penalty for people who refuse treatment
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of hospital supplies

explanation: You got it! A case definition gives healthcare workers clear, shared rules to correctly identify and count true cases during an outbreak. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h5)

question: What is a major cause of post-harvest food loss in farming communities?

options.A: Pest infestations and poor drying techniques
options.B: Strict international export inspections
options.C: Excessive government taxes on farm tools
options.D: Mandatory crop rotation laws from local councils

explanation: Bad storage, pests, and moisture can destroy a huge portion of crops right after harvest before they ever make it to market. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T18#GNS214_U1_T18_h4)

question: What should you do with the AED pads if the patient suddenly wakes up and starts breathing?

options.A: Move both pads to the patient's back to keep the skin warm
options.B: Peel them off immediately and throw them in the trash
options.C: Leave the pads attached to the chest in case arrest recurs
options.D: Wipe them down with bleach and pack them in the box

explanation: Leave the pads on! A recovered patient can still slip back into cardiac arrest very quickly, and you want the AED ready to go. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h7)

question: What term describes the study of what the body does to a drug (absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion)?

options.A: Pharmacokinetics
options.B: Pharmacogenetics
options.C: Pharmacodynamics
options.D: Pharmaceutics

explanation: Nailed it! Pharmacokinetics tracks the journey of the drug through the body across those four famous ADME stages. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T3#GNS125_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why do we measure blood pressure in millimeters of mercury (mmHg)?

options.A: It measures the exact weight of blood inside the heart
options.B: It estimates the total oxygen carried by red blood cells
options.C: It is the standard unit based on historical manometers
options.D: It calculates the chemical composition of plasma

explanation: It's all history! Early blood pressure tools (manometers) actually used columns of liquid mercury, and the mmHg unit stuck around to this day. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h1)

question: What happens if you use someone else's work without giving them credit?

options.A: Immediate acceptance into international journals
options.B: Automatic promotion in the clinical workplace
options.C: An increase in the statistical power of the study
options.D: Plagiarism and loss of professional credibility

explanation: Always give credit where it's due! Copying without referencing is plagiarism and hurts your professional reputation. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is an example of a posterior surface landmark?

options.A: Umbilicus
options.B: Inguinal crease

options.D: Maintaining strict patient confidentiality

question: How do deficiencies in calcium and vitamin D primarily contribute to fracture risk?

options.A: They increase sudden blood pressure spikes
options.B: They cause muscles to pull too hard on joints
options.C: They stop the bone from forming a blood clot
options.D: They impair proper bone mineralization and strength

explanation: Calcium and vitamin D are essential building blocks for strong bone matrix; without them, bones lose their structural density. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h4)

question: During a community disease outbreak, what is one of the main duties of a nurse?

options.A: Manufacturing new vaccines in the local clinic
options.B: Conducting contact tracing and health education
options.C: Prescribing experimental drugs without supervision
options.D: Changing national health budget allocations

explanation: As a nurse, you are a community educator and detective! You track down contacts and teach families how to stay safe and stop the spread. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T87#GNS214_U1_T87_h7)

question: A nurse checks clinic attendance registers to see which illnesses bring patients in most often. What is this called?

options.A: Reviewing epidemiological data
options.B: Performing environmental observation
options.C: Conducting cultural mapping
options.D: Establishing peer pressure groups

explanation: Spot on! Looking at clinic records to track disease patterns is a classic way we gather epidemiological data to plan our next steps. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why do doctors often order a full blood count (FBC) for a patient with heavy periods (menorrhagia)?

options.A: To look for a bacterial infection in the uterus
options.B: To see if the patient might get gestational diabetes
options.C: To check the levels of progesterone and estrogen
options.D: To check for low blood iron (anemia) caused by blood loss

explanation: Spot on! Heavy monthly bleeding can slowly drain the body's iron stores, leading to iron-deficiency anemia that needs our nursing care. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is considered the single most effective measure to prevent the spread of germs?

options.A: Avoiding all outdoor activities
options.B: Wearing heavy lead aprons
options.C: Taking daily multivitamins
options.D: Regular hand hygiene

explanation: Handwashing and hand sanitizing remove transient microorganisms, drastically reducing the transmission of infectious agents. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h6)

question: What does the psychosocial dimension in palliative care primarily focus on?

options.A: Surgical correction of terminal organs
options.B: Emotional, social, and psychological needs
options.C: Nutritional intake and calorie counting
options.D: Strict measurement of vital signs

explanation: Psychosocial care deals with the mental, emotional, and social well-being of the patient rather than purely physical functions. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard criterion for selecting an essential drug?

options.A: Bright packaging color and appealing flavor
options.B: High public health relevance
options.C: Proven clinical efficacy and safety
options.D: Acceptable cost-effectiveness

explanation: Aesthetic features like color and flavor do not determine whether a drug is medically essential for public health. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which set of signs makes up Cushing's triad, a warning sign of dangerous pressure on the brain stem?

options.A: Rapid heart rate, low blood pressure, and cold skin
options.B: Widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations
options.C: Pinpoint pupils, absent reflexes, and flaccid limbs
options.D: High fever, stiff neck, and sudden confusion

explanation: Cushing's triad is a classic nursing alert! Watch out for a wide pulse pressure (high systolic, low diastolic), a slow heart rate (bradycardia), and irregular breathing. It means pressure inside the head is dangerously high. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h6)

question: How did an iron lung primarily help a patient with respiratory paralysis breathe?

options.A: It used negative pressure to expand the chest wall
options.B: It compressed the abdomen to force air out of the lungs
options.C: It electrically stimulated the diaphragm to contract
options.D: It pumped high-pressure oxygen directly into the trachea

explanation: Iron lungs lowered air pressure inside the tank, causing the patient's chest to expand and air to rush into the lungs naturally. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of a performance appraisal in nursing management?

options.A: To find reasons to terminate employee contracts immediately
options.B: To replace daily clinical supervision entirely
options.C: To evaluate job performance and guide professional growth
options.D: To decide which nurse gets the biggest office space

explanation: Appraisals measure work against standards to help staff improve their clinical practice and develop professionally. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of recovery after a medical abortion?

options.A: Having light spotting that tapers off over a couple of weeks
options.B: Passing blood clots along with lower abdominal cramping
options.C: A persistent high fever starting several days after misoprostol
options.D: Experiencing mild nausea that goes away within twenty-four hours

explanation: A high fever is never normal—it's a warning sign of a potential infection that needs a doctor's attention right away. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T012#GNS226_U5_T012_h6)

question: What type of synovial joint allows you to move your shoulder and hip in almost every direction?

options.A: Ball-and-socket joint
options.B: Pivot joint
options.C: Hinge joint
options.D: Plane joint

explanation: Right on! Ball-and-socket joints (like your shoulder and hip) give you the widest range of motion in all directions. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T6#GNS121_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is a key action Nigerian nurses can take to promote male involvement?

options.A: Send police officers to bring absent fathers to the hospital
options.B: Ignore fathers in the waiting room to focus only on mothers
options.C: Actively invite men into consultation rooms and address both parents
options.D: Charge men extra fees for entering maternal health clinics

explanation: Nurses promote involvement by making fathers feel welcome and included in health discussions right from the start. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h7)

question: Why is it important for community health workers to know each other's roles clearly?

options.A: To reduce the number of home visits required each week
options.B: To prevent missed tasks and avoid doing the exact same work
options.C: To allow nurses to prescribe medications legally
options.D: To ensure doctors maintain authority over all other workers

explanation: Well done! Knowing who does what keeps care smooth and ensures no important patient need slips through the cracks. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h3)

question: Why is a discharge plan likely to fail if it ignores a patient's home life and financial situation?

options.A: Because medications work better when prescribed without social context
options.B: Because the patient may not be able to afford or follow the recommended instructions at home
options.C: Because nurses are only responsible for care inside the hospital gates
options.D: Because hospital management automatically cancels plans made without doctor approval

explanation: Exactly! If a care plan doesn't fit what the patient can actually afford or do at home, they won't be able to stick to it. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T15#GNS312_U4_T15_h7)

question: What is the main trigger that causes blood vessels in the newborn lungs to relax and open?

options.A: Gravity pulling fluid downward
options.B: The sudden release of adrenal hormones
options.C: The physical drop in environmental temperature
options.D: Exposure to oxygen from the first breath

explanation: Oxygen is a powerful natural vasodilator; when air enters the lungs, the sudden oxygen increase relaxes the pulmonary blood vessels. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h3)

question: Why do advanced emphysema patients often end up with a flattened diaphragm and hard-working breathing muscles?

options.A: Scar tissue in the pleural lining pulls the diaphragm upward into the neck
options.B: Loss of pulmonary blood flow weakens the intercostal muscle fibers
options.C: Thick mucus plugs block the trachea and force the chest wall to expand
options.D: Air trapping hyperinflates the lungs and pushes the diaphragm downward

explanation: Makes total sense! Trapped air keeps the chest inflated like a balloon, flattening the diaphragm and making it tired and less efficient. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why do heavy blocks of text usually fail in community health education programs?

options.A: People prefer listening to long audio recordings instead.
options.B: Ink tends to smudge when paragraphs are printed too close together.
options.C: Medical authorities forbid the use of written sentences on posters.
options.D: Low literacy rates in the target population make reading difficult.

explanation: Many community members have limited reading skills. If your poster is packed with heavy text, the main health message gets lost. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h3)

question: When scrubbing and rinsing your arms, which direction should you always go?

options.A: Beginning at your upper arm and moving down
options.B: From your elbows down toward your fingertips
options.C: Starting at your wrists and moving in circles
options.D: From your fingertips up toward your elbows

explanation: Always move from the cleanest part (fingertips) to the less clean part (elbows). Easy to remember! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the main use of the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) in the ward?

options.A: To test the patient's long-term memory
options.B: To diagnose the exact cause of a brain injury
options.C: To check the strength of peripheral nerves
options.D: To measure a patient's level of consciousness

explanation: You'll use the GCS every day on clinical placement! It gives us a quick, reliable way to check and record how alert a patient is. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T7#GNS222_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why is checking nutritional status such an important part of nursing care for HIV patients?

options.A: Vitamins are the only treatment needed for early-stage disease
options.B: Poor nutrition prevents the skin from absorbing medications
options.C: Dietary changes can completely cure the viral infection
options.D: Wasting syndrome and chronic diarrhea frequently threaten recovery

explanation: Spot on. Good nutrition keeps the immune system strong, while complications like wasting and diarrhea can quickly pull a patient down. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h6)

question: Which of these substances can interfere with platelet function and raise a patient's risk of bleeding?

options.A: Inhaled medications for mild asthma
options.B: Prescribed eye drops for glaucoma
options.C: Herbal supplements like garlic and ginkgo
options.D: Standard daily multivitamins with calcium

explanation: Some common herbal supplements act like natural blood thinners. Always ask patients about herbs and supplements they take at home! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T2#GNS311_U2_T2_h6)

question: What crucial information must you always write down in a patient's referral note?

options.A: The religious affiliation and family history of the patient
options.B: A detailed breakdown of transport costs incurred by the family
options.C: The personal phone number of the community health officer
options.D: Vital signs, suspected diagnosis, and treatment given so far

explanation: The receiving doctors need a quick cheat sheet! Always include current vital signs, what you think is wrong, and any drugs or fluids you've already given. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h6)

question: Which oxygen delivery device is best for providing an exact, controlled percentage of oxygen to a patient?

options.A: Non-rebreather bag
options.B: Standard nasal cannula
options.C: Venturi mask
options.D: Simple face mask

explanation: The Venturi mask uses special adapter barrels to mix room air and oxygen precisely, delivering a specific, reliable oxygen percentage. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h5)

question: A woman who had FGM as a child comes in for delivery. What major complication is she most at risk for?

options.A: Complete absence of uterine contractions throughout the first stage
options.B: Obstructed labor due to severe scar tissue and rigid tissue narrowing
options.C: Sudden development of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Premature closure of the infant's fontanelles inside the womb

explanation: Spot on! Thick scar tissue from FGM doesn't stretch easily, making it very hard for the baby to pass through smoothly during childbirth. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T1#GNS312_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why do nurses encourage patients to walk around soon after a laparoscopy?

options.A: It helps expel trapped gas and prevents blood clots
options.B: It ensures the patient can immediately leave the hospital
options.C: It replaces the need for prescribed pain medications
options.D: It prevents the surgical incisions from opening up

explanation: Brilliant! Early walking gets the blood moving in the legs to stop clots and helps the body clear out that trapped tummy gas faster. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of a community-centred food supply system?

options.A: Regional self-reliance and local connections
options.B: International cargo shipping and bulk trade
options.C: Relying entirely on imported food items
options.D: Industrial food processing and long storage

explanation: Spot on! Community-centred systems are all about linking local farmers directly with nearby folks to build strong, self-reliant regions. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T030#GNS227_U2_T030_h1)

question: Why might a patient be given oral contrast before a CT scan?

options.A: To numb the lining of the throat for comfort
options.B: To outline the stomach and intestines clearly
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure during the test
options.D: To prevent allergic reactions to intravenous dye

explanation: Swallowing oral contrast helps coat the gut so doctors can easily spot issues like blockages. Simple and smart! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h2)

question: Which of these everyday lifestyle habits can negatively impact fertility in both men and women?

options.A: Natural age-related decline
options.B: Genetic chromosome makeup
options.C: Congenital uterine anomalies
options.D: Cigarette smoking

explanation: Brilliant! Smoking is a habit patients can actually change, and it directly hurts both sperm quality and ovarian health. You're mastering this! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h2)

question: How should a nurse approach a terminally ill patient experiencing deep sadness in the depression stage?

options.A: Request an immediate psychiatric consult for clinical antidepressants
options.B: Distract the patient with busy hospital activities and television
options.C: Encourage the patient to cheer up and focus on positive thoughts
options.D: Provide a quiet, supportive presence and allow expression of grief

explanation: Sadness at this stage is a normal reaction, so offering a comforting presence is more helpful than trying to force artificial cheer. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of keeping accurate records of workplace injuries and close calls?

options.A: It helps identify dangerous trends and prevents future accidents
options.B: It guarantees that the business will never face taxation
options.C: It allows employers to hide safety violations from inspectors
options.D: It replaces the need to provide medical treatment to victims

explanation: Reviewing past injury logs helps safety teams spot repeating problems so they can fix them before anyone else gets hurt. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h8)

question: Which viral enzyme helps convert HIV's single-stranded RNA into double-stranded DNA?

options.A: Integrase
options.B: Amylase
options.C: Reverse transcriptase
options.D: Protease

explanation: Reverse transcriptase is the clever enzyme HIV uses to turn its RNA into DNA inside the host cell. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h2)

question: How long must symptoms last before a doctor or nurse can clinically diagnose female sexual dysfunction?

options.A: At least six months
options.B: At least two weeks
options.C: Twelve months straight
options.D: One month or more

explanation: You've got this! Because temporary stress happens to everyone, clinicians look for symptoms to last at least six months along with personal distress before making a diagnosis. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T25#GNS312_U1_T25_h1)

question: Which communication channel is best suited for building deep trust and allowing immediate feedback with a patient?

options.A: A prerecorded radio jingle
options.B: Interpersonal communication
options.C: A national television advertisement
options.D: A billboard on a major highway

explanation: Nothing beats face-to-face talk! Interpersonal communication lets you clear doubts, answer questions directly, and build wonderful rapport with your patients. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h4)

question: Which gland produces melatonin to help control your sleep cycle?

options.A: Pituitary gland
options.B: Thyroid gland
options.C: Pineal gland
options.D: Adrenal gland

explanation: That's correct! The pineal gland senses darkness and releases melatonin to help you wind down for sleep. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of using direct observation during a community survey?

options.A: It replaces the need to ever talk to local political leaders
options.B: It eliminates the need for any data analysis or calculations
options.C: It allows the nurse to see actual living and environmental conditions firsthand
options.D: It guarantees that no member of the community will fall sick

explanation: Observation lets nurses witness reality directly without relying on what people say or what old records report. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which service is a key part of disease prevention in comprehensive health care?

options.A: Performing major open-heart surgeries
options.B: Giving routine immunizations to children
options.C: Importing expensive specialized drugs
options.D: Building high-rise luxury hospitals

explanation: Immunizations stop preventable infectious diseases from spreading through a community, making them a core preventive service. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: You see blood sugar numbers in a table, but the column header forgot to state the measurement units. What is your best move?

options.A: Write your own arbitrary units into the published article
options.B: Ignore the table completely because it is completely useless
options.C: Check the footnotes or surrounding text to find the missing units of measurement
options.D: Guess that the values are measured in standard international units

explanation: Don't panic! Researchers usually hide missing units down in the footnotes or explain them right inside the nearby paragraphs. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h5)

question: What must the urinary sphincters do so that normal urination can happen?

options.A: They must contract tightly
options.B: They must relax
options.C: They must spasm
options.D: They must thicken

explanation: For urine to flow out smoothly, the urinary sphincters need to open up (relax) at the same time the bladder muscle squeezes. Teamwork! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h2)

question: Why is setting up an IV line so crucial during a resuscitation?

options.A: To secure the endotracheal tube in place
options.B: To measure the exact volume of carbon dioxide exhaled
options.C: To monitor the patient's core body temperature
options.D: To deliver emergency medications and fluids directly into the bloodstream

explanation: Spot on! An IV line acts like a fast highway to pump life-saving drugs straight into circulation when every second counts. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a challenge that leads to unsafe injection practices in low-resource settings?

options.A: High patient demand for parenteral treatments
options.B: Shortages of single-use sterile injection equipment
options.C: An overabundance of certified auto-disable syringes
options.D: The operation of informal and unregulated drug vendors

explanation: Facilities actually suffer from shortages of safe equipment, not an overabundance! Lack of supplies is a major hurdle. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h5)

question: What dangerous illness is linked closely to improperly canned low-acid foods?

options.A: Malaria
options.B: Tuberculosis
options.C: Botulism
options.D: Cholera

explanation: Poor canning can create an airtight space where the germ *Clostridium botulinum* loves to grow and make a dangerous, paralyzing toxin. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h7)

question: Which type of range of motion exercise requires the patient to move their own joints to build strength?

options.A: Continuous passive motion
options.B: Active range of motion
options.C: Passive range of motion
options.D: Static stretching motion

explanation: Spot on! *Active* range of motion means the patient uses their own muscles, which helps maintain both joint flexibility and muscle strength. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main difference between vaccine efficacy and vaccine effectiveness?

options.A: Effectiveness applies only to viral vaccines while efficacy applies to bacterial vaccines
options.B: Effectiveness is determined in a laboratory before animal testing begins
options.C: Efficacy measures performance in ideal trials while effectiveness measures performance in everyday settings
options.D: Efficacy is measured in children while effectiveness is measured in adults

explanation: Think of efficacy as how a vaccine performs in a controlled lab test, while effectiveness is how it holds up for real people out in the community! You've got this. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T70#GNS214_U1_T70_h1)

question: A mother feels defensive when asked about her child's diet. What approach should the nurse use?

options.A: Use open-ended, non-judgmental questions to explore current practices
options.B: Hand her a detailed textbook and ask her to read it alone
options.C: Report the mother immediately to the hospital social worker
options.D: Scold the mother so she takes the nutritional advice more seriously

explanation: Empathy goes a long way! Asking open, friendly questions builds trust so mothers feel safe sharing their true feeding challenges. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h8)

question: What does health literacy refer to in nursing practice?

options.A: The number of medical books a patient has read at home
options.B: A person's ability to understand and use basic health information
options.C: How fast a client can write down their doctor's name
options.D: The level of education the nurse completed in school

explanation: Health literacy is the practical skill of understanding medical instructions, prescriptions, and health advice. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h3)

question: You keep checking your phone while a patient is trying to tell you about their pain. What message does this send?

options.A: Using excessive medical jargon during the assessment
options.B: Failing to establish the correct termination phase
options.C: Stereotyping the patient's cultural background
options.D: Showing impatience and making the patient feel like a burden

explanation: Rushing or splitting your attention makes the patient feel ignored and destroys trust. Always give them your full presence! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h5)

question: A nurse only checks clinic records to decide what health program to build. What is the biggest downside to this?

options.A: It is too expensive for hospital computers
options.B: It stops doctors from writing prescriptions
options.C: It takes too many years to gather basic stats
options.D: It misses vulnerable people who never make it to the clinic

explanation: You got it! Clinic records only show those who could reach the facility. You might completely miss sick people who are too far away or can't afford transport. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h3)

question: In cervical cell changes, what makes CIN 3 more serious than the earlier stages?

options.A: The viral infection has completely cleared from the body
options.B: Dysplastic cells are confined strictly to the basal cell layer
options.C: Invasion through the basement membrane has already occurred
options.D: Severe dysplasia spans almost the entire thickness of the epithelium

explanation: You're learning fast! CIN 3 means the abnormal (dysplastic) changes have spread across almost the whole thickness of the surface tissue. The good news at this stage is that it hasn't broken through the basement membrane yet. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h3)

question: Who introduced the concept of 'total pain' in palliative care?

options.A: Virginia Henderson
options.B: Dame Cicely Saunders
options.C: Jean Watson
options.D: Florence Nightingale

explanation: Props to Dame Cicely Saunders! She pioneered modern hospice care and taught us that pain isn't just physical—it touches our emotions and spirit too. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h4)

question: A patient looks dizzy and pale right after having blood drawn for a screening. What should you do first?

options.A: Tell the patient to lie flat on the floor and leave them alone
options.B: Wait for thirty minutes without taking any action
options.C: Ask the patient to walk quickly to the exit to get fresh air
options.D: Have the patient sit down with their head low and offer water or a snack

explanation: Well done! Dizziness after fasting blood work is common. Sitting down and taking fluids helps steady their blood sugar and pressure. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T5#GNS123_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which mineral helps a new mother beat fatigue and rebuild iron stores lost during childbirth?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Potassium
options.D: Iron

explanation: Iron builds hemoglobin, helping mums recover from delivery blood loss and keeping postpartum fatigue and anemia at bay. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h4)

question: A community health nurse checks local clinic records to see which neighborhoods have the highest asthma rates in children. Why is this so helpful?

options.A: To prove that childhood illnesses are impossible to prevent
options.B: To penalize local clinics that failed to cure their patients
options.C: To target prevention and education programs where they are needed most
options.D: To stop families from moving into polluted urban areas

explanation: Resources are always limited, so finding out exactly where a disease hits hardest lets nurses focus their education and support where it will do the most good. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T1#GNS313_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why must you NEVER use a tongue depressor to check the throat of a child you suspect has acute epiglottitis?

options.A: It causes severe pain in the gums
options.B: It interferes with accurate pulse oximetry
options.C: It can trigger sudden total airway closure
options.D: It makes the fever spike higher immediately

explanation: Well done! Pressing down on an already swollen, angry epiglottis can cause sudden muscle spasms and completely block the child's airway. Safety first—leave it alone! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T5#GNS311_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the most important nursing check right after a patient has a liver biopsy?

options.A: Remove all intravenous access lines right away
options.B: Monitor vital signs and check the puncture site for bleeding
options.C: Feed the patient a large high-fiber meal immediately
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk briskly around the hospital ward

explanation: Since the liver has a huge blood supply, watching closely for bleeding and checking vital signs is top priority after this procedure. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h5)

question: You are about to give oral digoxin, but your adult patient's apical pulse is 52 beats per minute. What should you do?

options.A: Withhold the dose and notify the prescriber
options.B: Encourage exercise to raise the pulse before giving it
options.C: Give half the dose now and half in six hours
options.D: Administer the medication as prescribed immediately

explanation: Brilliant clinical judgement! Always remember: if an adult patient's pulse is below 60, hold the digoxin and check in with the doctor to keep your patient safe from toxicity. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which type of diarrhoea happens when inflammation causes blood, pus, and mucus to leak into the bowel?

options.A: Osmotic diarrhoea
options.B: Secretory diarrhoea
options.C: Exudative diarrhoea
options.D: Motility diarrhoea

explanation: When the gut lining gets inflamed and 'weeps' fluid, blood, or mucus—like in a bad infection or IBD—we call it exudative diarrhoea. Great nursing vocabulary to keep in your toolkit! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h2)

question: In family planning, what do we mean by 'typical use' of a birth control method?

options.A: How effectively the method works during everyday, real-life use
options.B: The percentage of people who choose the method on their first visit
options.C: How well the method works when applied correctly every single time
options.D: The laboratory score assigned by the manufacturing pharmaceutical company

explanation: Spot on! 'Typical use' accounts for real life—meaning human errors, busy schedules, or slip-ups that happen outside a lab. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h4)

question: What is the main difference between a vaccine contraindication and a precaution?

options.A: A contraindication greatly increases the risk of a serious adverse reaction
options.B: A precaution means the vaccine will definitely cause immediate death
options.C: A contraindication only applies to adult travelers and never infants
options.D: A precaution requires doubling the standard pediatric vaccine dose

explanation: Contraindications mean the risk of harm clearly outweighs any potential benefit, making the vaccine unsafe to administer. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h3)

question: Why is writing a proposal considered a necessary step for nurse researchers?

question: What is the main purpose of the Beers Criteria?

question: When taking a family history, which relatives are most important to include?

question: Why does high prolactin stop a woman from releasing an egg during ovulation?

question: Within how many hours must a single unit of packed red blood cells be completely infused?

question: Before the treaty, why did companies love to ship toxic waste to other countries?

question: What is the main job of progesterone during pregnancy?

question: Why is NGO advocacy for vulnerable populations so important in public health?

options.C: It influences policymakers to prioritize resources for underserved groups

question: What post-procedure instruction should a nurse give to a patient who just received a knee injection?

question: Why do the remaining healthy nephrons get larger (hypertrophy) during the early stages of chronic kidney disease?

question: Which metabolic pathway breaks down large molecules and releases energy?

options.A: Homeostasis
options.B: Anabolism
options.C: Osmosis
options.D: Catabolism

explanation: Remember: Catabolism cuts things down! It tears complex molecules into simpler pieces, releasing energy for your body to use. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h2)

question: What type of question should you ask if you want a patient to open up and share their feelings?

options.A: Rhetorical question

options.D: Leading question

explanation: Open-ended questions give patients the freedom to talk in their own words, rather than just answering a quick 'yes' or 'no'. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main reason for taking a swab (culture and sensitivity) from an infected ear or throat?

options.D: To bring down swelling and open up airways

question: When amino acids are broken down, they produce toxic ammonia. How does the body safely get rid of it?

options.B: The lungs exhale it immediately as a dry nitrogen gas vapor
options.C: The liver converts it into urea for safe removal by the kidneys
options.D: The stomach uses it directly to neutralize strong gastric acids

question: Why are lower respiratory infections generally more serious than upper respiratory ones?

options.C: They directly interfere with oxygen exchange in the air sacs.

question: A primary nurse notices a prescribed drug dose does not match a patient's failing kidneys. What is the best action?

question: Which of these conditions can cause sudden swelling of the soft tissues in the upper airway?

question: Which of these is NOT a valid reason to delay vaccinating a sick child?

question: A patient with active TB is on the ward. Which nursing action directly targets the human reservoir?

options.C: Providing emotional counselling on chronic illness
options.D: Administering the prescribed anti-tuberculosis medications

question: What is the main job of sensory receptors in our special senses?

options.A: Pump blood through the sensory organs
options.B: Convert environmental stimuli into electrical signals

options.D: Produce hormones to regulate body temperature

explanation: Think of sensory receptors as tiny translators! They take physical things from the world around us—like light or sound—and change them into electrical signals that our nervous system can easily read and understand. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the best tool to use for smoothing out rough nail edges after clipping?

question: What is the main job of H2-receptor blockers in the stomach?

question: As a community health nurse, why should you treat pregnant women and under-five children as a priority group?

question: What is the anatomical term for a joint where two or more bones meet?

question: Blood pooling in the legs from long-term bed rest can lead to which major vascular complication?

question: How does incidence differ from prevalence in community health data?

options.A: Incidence counts deaths, while prevalence counts active infections

options.C: Incidence measures new cases over time, while prevalence measures total existing cases
options.D: Incidence only applies to children, while prevalence applies to adults

question: A woman with vasa previa goes into early labor and her water breaks. What is the biggest, most urgent danger to the baby?

question: How does a pregnant woman's total blood volume usually change during a normal pregnancy?

question: How many loose or watery stools in a day is officially considered diarrhoea?

question: What activity rule should you teach a patient before they go home after a liver biopsy?

question: What is a vital safety item a patient living with diabetes should always carry around?

question: Which measurements do nurses routinely track to monitor a patient's progress on a low-calorie diet?

question: What is the primary purpose of a unit dose cart on a hospital ward?

question: Why do prescription medications require a doctor's order?

question: Why must a nurse assess a patient's cultural food preferences before creating a diabetic meal plan?

question: What heart rate defines sinus tachycardia in an adult?

question: What is the most important assessment when checking a limb's circulation and nerve function after a joint procedure?

question: Why is checking a patient's current medications so important during a sexual health assessment?

question: Why do certain long-term medications often lead to bad tooth decay?

question: Why can missing certain body enzymes lead to cell damage when taking a drug?

question: Between which two meningeal layers is the subarachnoid space located?

question: What is the main advantage of a self-retaining retractor like the Weitlaner?

question: What is a key role of the community health nurse in home delivery selection?

question: What is the primary public health way to prevent iodine deficiency in a population?

question: A nurse finds a 5-year-old child with sudden, floppy weakness in both legs. What is the best immediate nursing response?

question: What does the concept of universal precautions mean in clinical practice?

question: Which of these is NOT checked during a standard surgical time-out?

question: What is the main goal of teaching Kegel exercises to someone with urinary incontinence?

question: How does the lower oesophageal sphincter keep itself tightly closed to stop acid reflux?

question: Why does the nurse keep one hand hovering closely over an infant while they are on the scale pan?

options.C: To prevent the baby from falling off the scale
options.D: To stop the digital numbers from fluctuating

question: Why is relying heavily on staff overtime a poor long-term way to save money?

options.A: Overtime is usually paid at a higher premium rate and leads to staff burnout
options.B: Overtime payments are never recorded in the unit operational budget
options.C: Working extra hours causes nurses to forget all their clinical training
options.D: Overtime hours are completely illegal under standard hospital labor laws

question: Which of the following is an example of vector-borne transmission?

options.B: A mosquito transmitting the malaria parasite to a human
options.C: Drinking water contaminated with cholera bacteria
options.D: Acquiring a skin infection through direct contact with a sore

question: What is the primary goal of immediate first aid for a suspected fracture?

options.C: Straighten the deformed limb immediately by pulling hard
options.D: Immobilize the bone to prevent further tissue damage

question: Why can taking a health history for hormone problems be tricky for a nurse?

options.C: Endocrine problems only affect one specific body system at a time
options.D: Laboratory tests are completely useless without a physical exam

question: Where do water-soluble (peptide) hormone receptors usually sit?

options.A: On the outer cell membrane
options.B: Attached directly to cellular DNA
options.C: Inside the cell nucleus
options.D: Floating freely in the cytoplasm

question: How should you as a nurse organize your questions when running through a review of systems?

options.C: Ask the patient to list every illness they had as a child

question: What is the quickest and most practical way for a nurse to check what a patient has eaten recently during a busy clinic day?

options.C: Asking for a 24-hour dietary recall
options.D: Ordering a full metabolic blood panel

question: How do home care nurses help prevent clients from ending up back in the hospital?

options.D: By admitting the client to a nursing home immediately

question: What is the biggest benefit of practicing patient-centred care?

question: When washing a patient's arms or legs during a bed bath, why does the nurse stroke from the hands or feet toward the torso?

question: Where do the majority of the lymphatic vessels of the breast drain?

question: What is a major misconception regarding adolescent mental health and self-harm?

options.A: Depression in teenagers always manifests as persistent sadness and crying
